title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker

nodes.name: Player ground movement and target-lock movement
nodes.purpose: Stick-driven run speed and heading for the player character, plus the separate strafe and back-step speed sets used while a target is locked. Every tuning value sits in a positional data table whose fields are unnamed in the source, so the meanings here come from how the code uses each field.

nodes.name: Player jump, fall, landing, roll and evasive hops
nodes.purpose: Launch, gravity, terminal speed, landing reactions, forward roll, back flip and side hop. Velocity is integrated once per update. Tuning values come from the same unnamed positional tables.

nodes.name: Ledge detection by height
nodes.purpose: Classifies the wall in front of the player by ledge height and picks a small hop, a wall catch or a vertical jump after the stick has pushed on the wall for a few updates.

nodes.name: Swimming
nodes.purpose: Water entry, swim speed and heading, and the surfacing test.

nodes.name: Sword combo chain
nodes.purpose: Chooses the next sword attack from a chain counter and the stick direction, and sets hit strength.

nodes.name: Timed parry counter attacks
nodes.purpose: While locked on to a hostile target the player can answer an enemy attack window with a jump slash, a circling roll slash or a vertical jump slash.

nodes.name: Leaf glide
nodes.purpose: Slow descent with wind drift, a magic cost and steering from the stick.

nodes.name: Grappling hook
nodes.purpose: A chain tip that flies in a line, sticks to marked surfaces to pull the player in, or hooks small actors and drags them back.

nodes.name: Multi-target boomerang
nodes.purpose: A thrown projectile that visits up to five locked targets, turns toward each, then returns to the thrower.

nodes.name: Target lock selection and release
nodes.purpose: Scores nearby actors for lock-on and action prompts with a distance table, a front-cone test and an angle-weighted distance, then keeps the lock until the release radius is passed.

nodes.name: Lock-on camera
nodes.purpose: Third-person camera that frames the player and the locked target, swings out when the view is blocked, and drops a forced lock when the target is far or old.

nodes.name: Global wind direction and strength
nodes.purpose: Holds one world wind vector and strength. A stage sets a base strength level and a song or event sets the direction. The value eases toward its target.

nodes.name: Ocean surface height field
nodes.purpose: A grid of heights that follows the player, built from four traveling waves. Any actor can ask for the surface height at a point.

nodes.name: Sailing boat
nodes.purpose: Wind-driven boat speed, tiller turning, wave riding, sail jump, crash knock-off and the deck cannon.

cards.name: Run speed from squared stick push, with a gated acceleration
cards.summary: The target run speed is the top speed times the stick push squared. Acceleration only applies while the stick is beyond a threshold that rises with current speed, and it falls to zero when the stick points away from the heading.
cards.behavior: Each update the ground target speed is top speed times stick distance times stick distance, so a half push gives a quarter of top speed. During scripted events, while carrying a heavy object or wearing heavy boots, the target is linear in the stick instead. A stick push below a small dead zone gives no acceleration. Above it, acceleration is a gain times the squared stick push times the alignment between the stick direction and the current heading. Alignment is floored at 0.7 once the character is above half of top speed, and at 0 below that. The stick must also exceed half of one minus the speed ratio, so near top speed a light push gives no acceleration and the character coasts. When current speed is above the target, speed falls toward the target by a fraction of the gap per update, limited between a minimum and a maximum step. Pushing straight into a wall cuts the target speed by the wall-scrape factor times the cosine of the wall angle. The heading chases the stick direction by one fifth of the remaining error per update, capped by a maximum step scaled with the squared push. If the stick flips to almost the opposite direction while moving, the normal heading chase is skipped. At speed the function returns early, and at low speed it turns the heading toward the stick. The slip and turn-around moves handle the rest.

cards.name: Locked-on strafe and back-step speed sets
cards.summary: While a target is locked the player uses a slower strafe speed set and a separate back-step set, each with its own acceleration, braking and turn rate. Facing follows the target, not the stick.
cards.behavior: When a lock is held on an actor, the maximum speed switches from the free-run value to the strafe value for every direction, and the character faces the target while the movement heading follows the stick. When the lock button is held with no actor to lock, the code reads the cosine between the movement heading and the facing. At or above the forward threshold the normal run set applies. At or below the backward threshold a back-step set applies with its own maximum and acceleration. Anything between uses the strafe set. If the movement heading points backward relative to the facing, the heading is flipped by 180 degrees and the speed sign is flipped, so the character reverses without turning through a half circle. Heading chases the stick direction by one sixth of the error per update, with a large minimum step so strafing feels crisp.

cards.name: Run-speed-scaled jump launch at a fixed angle
cards.summary: A jump is a fixed-angle launch whose power is the run speed, clamped to a minimum, times a gain. A standing jump therefore equals a slow run jump. Mid-air control is a gentle chase toward the run speed.
cards.behavior: At takeoff the forward speed is clamped between a minimum takeoff speed and the top run speed. The launch velocity is that clamped speed times a gain, split by a fixed angle of about 60 degrees into horizontal and vertical parts. For a full-speed jump this gives roughly 13 units per update forward and 23 units per update up. For a minimum-speed jump it gives roughly 7 forward and 12.5 up. In the air, forward speed chases the top run speed with a small step per update. A separate braking branch exists for the case where a carried object has just been let go: it pulls forward speed toward zero by a step scaled with the stick push, or by a tenth of that with no push. Gravity pulls the vertical speed down by a fixed amount per update until it reaches the terminal speed. The jump animation switches to its falling pose once the downward speed passes the gravity step.

cards.name: Gravity, heavy-boot gravity and three landing tiers
cards.summary: Gravity is a constant step per update with a terminal speed. Heavy boots multiply gravity and the cap. Landing reaction depends on the drop from the apex of the fall, in three tiers, with a roll-out for long forward falls.
cards.behavior: Each update vertical speed gains the gravity step and is clamped at the terminal speed. When the heavy state is on, the gravity step is multiplied and the terminal speed is multiplied too. The fall height is measured from the apex of the last upward motion, or from the start of the fall. On landing, a drop of at least one half of the light threshold gives a mild landing reaction. A drop at or above the light threshold gives the middle reaction, and a drop at or above the heavy threshold gives the strongest reaction. Giant-flower surfaces skip these reactions. If the stick is pushed forward and past half, the drop from the start of the air time is at least 300 units, and the facing is forward, the character rolls out of the landing at top run speed instead.

cards.name: Forward roll with speed carry and wall crash
cards.summary: The roll speed is derived from the speed on entry, with a floor and a ceiling. A roll can be cancelled late, and it crashes into a wall when it is fast enough and the wall is hit inside a frame window.
cards.behavior: On entry the roll speed is entry speed times a gain plus a bonus, so a full-speed roll is faster than a run. It is floored at a minimum roll speed, and capped at top run speed times the gain plus the bonus. Heavy gear scales it down. When the roll animation ends with the stick released, the carried speed is lowered by the minimum roll speed. After a cancel frame the roll accepts the next action. If entry speed was at least a threshold and the character hits a wall roughly facing it between two animation frames, the roll turns into a stumble that keeps a fraction of the speed.

cards.name: Back flip and side hop launch vectors
cards.summary: The back flip and the target-lock side hop are short ballistic jumps with fixed speeds and their own gravity. The back flip falls out into a normal fall if the ground drops away.
cards.behavior: The back flip launches backward at a fixed horizontal speed and a fixed vertical speed under its own gravity, which makes a flight of about 13 updates and about 285 units of travel (derived from the numbers). Heavy gear halves the horizontal speed. If the character falls more than a set distance below the start height, the flip hands over to the normal fall. The side hop launches sideways from the facing at a fixed total speed split by a fixed angle of about 34 degrees (roughly 25 units per update sideways and 17 up), with a lower gravity. While it runs, facing turns toward the locked target.

cards.name: Ledge reaction chosen by ledge height
cards.summary: The height of the ledge above the feet picks the reaction: a small hop, a hang-and-pull, or a jump up. The stick must push on the wall for a few updates first.
cards.behavior: A forward probe finds the wall and the ledge top. The ledge height above the feet is compared with four bands. Below a minimum nothing happens. Up to the first band the character makes a small hop up. Up to the second band it catches the wall and pulls up. Up to the third and above it makes a vertical jump to reach the ledge. A ledge above the highest reach is ignored. The reaction fires only after the stick has pushed against the wall for a count of consecutive updates, which is smaller for small hops than for the other two. In mid-air the character grabs a ledge and hangs only when the ledge top is more than 125 units above the ground under the player. While carrying an object, ledges above the first band are ignored.

cards.name: Swim speed, depth trigger and entry splash
cards.summary: Swimming starts when the water is deeper than a fixed depth over the feet. Swim speed has a cap, a stick-driven acceleration and a slow decay. A locked target scales the cap by the facing angle.
cards.behavior: Swimming begins when the water surface is more than a depth threshold above the feet. If the character was falling, the entry keeps the old vertical speed (clamped between a floor and zero) and keeps three quarters of the horizontal speed. Free swimming sets the cap, adds acceleration of stick push times a gain times the heading alignment, and decays toward the target by a small fraction with a step range. The facing turns toward the stick by one seventeenth of the error per update, with a step range. With a target locked the cap is scaled between half and the full value, from the angle between the movement heading and the facing, so moving sideways or backward is slower. Without a lock, a stick pointing opposite to the facing snaps both facing and heading to the stick direction. With a lock, swimming backward gives no acceleration and the speed is zeroed below a threshold before the heading resets.

cards.name: Sword combo chain picked by counter and stick direction
cards.summary: Each press of the sword button advances a chain counter. Counts one to three give directional slashes, four gives a finisher, and five and six open stronger variants that depend on the stick direction.
cards.behavior: The chain counter rises by one on each chained attack. For counts below four, the stick direction relative to the target (or to the current facing when no target is locked) chooses between a forward-stick, a right-stick or a left-stick slash. With no stick push, a locked player gets a neutral slash and an unlocked player gets the left slash. At four the player does the finisher: one version for forward or right, another for the rest. At five the stick picks a leaping extra slash for forward, a diagonal slash for right and another extra slash for the others. At six forward gives a turning slash, no push gives a second extra slash and the sides give the leaping slash in two variants. Before the chain advances, a parry-ready state can replace the next slash with the counter attack of the parry card. Hit strength is one for the base blade and two for the upgraded blade, doubled again for a finishing slash. A slash that hits a wall or a shield rebounds into a recoil move.

cards.name: Parry counter: attack window, solved jump arc, circling roll
cards.summary: An enemy announces a timed attack window and a counter type. The prompt shows slightly before the window opens. A press at or after the window start launches a jump slash on a solved arc, a circling roll slash, or a vertical jump slash.
cards.behavior: Each hostile target publishes an attack type, a start frame, an end frame, a trigger distance, a body radius and a hit height. While locked on with the sword drawn, the parry prompt shows once the target frame is within a small lead before the start frame and before the end frame, and the target is within the trigger distance on the ground plane. The counter fires on a press at or after the start frame. For a jump slash the arc is solved: the apex height is the target height difference plus the hit height, floored at a minimum, and the flight time follows from that height and the arc gravity. Vertical speed is gravity times that time, and horizontal speed is the flat distance over that time. After the slash the player hops off with a fixed up speed, forward speed and gravity. The roll counter circles by a little under half a turn around the midpoint between the player and a point just in front of the enemy, and ends on the far side. The vertical jump and the last-combo wait are the other two attack types.

cards.name: Leaf glide with soft fall, wind drift and magic drain
cards.summary: Opening the leaf mid-air sets a lift speed and then limits the fall to a slow terminal speed. Forward speed follows the stick up to a cap and wind pushes the player. Magic drains on a timer and landing or a cancel ends the glide.
cards.behavior: On the first glide update the vertical speed is set to a positive lift and, for the standard start, the forward speed is set to the glide cap. After that gravity is weak and the fall speed is clamped at a slow terminal value. Forward speed chases the stick push times the glide cap, scaled by the cosine of the stick angle off the facing, with a step that grows with the push. The yaw rate target is 512 binary angle units times the push times the sine of that angle, reached with a small step limit. The world wind vector, scaled by a gain and by a strength factor that saturates at one, adds a drift each update, eased in with a step cap. A hit by a wind source replaces that drift with the hit vector, capped at 50 units. One magic point drains every fixed number of updates, and the glide ends when magic runs out or the player cancels after a short lockout. Heavy boots skip the lift and the caps.

cards.name: Grappling hook: fixed-speed flight, range and chain reel
cards.summary: The hook tip flies in a straight line a fixed distance each update. It sticks to marked surfaces and reels the player in, or hooks actors and carries them back. The reel runs a fixed number of chain links per update.
cards.behavior: The tip first checks a short segment behind its launch point. If that is already blocked the shot returns at once. Otherwise each update the tip sweeps a capsule from its position to a point a set number of direction steps ahead, and then moves to the end of the sweep. With a step of 7 units and 15 steps the tip moves 105 units per update (derived). The shot ends at a maximum distance from the hand, at a wall that cannot be gripped (it bounces and returns), or at a hit actor. A surface flagged as grippable, or an actor flagged as a pull point, switches the system to a pull: the chain is measured in links of 7 units, and each update reels up to 9 links, or 63 units, until fewer links remain. A hit actor that is flagged as carryable instead rides the returning chain and is kept on the ground by a ground probe. The return phase reels 63 units per update too.

cards.name: Boomerang: multi-lock route, curved free throw, range and return
cards.summary: The boomerang flies at a fixed speed to up to five locked targets in order, steering with a turn limit that tightens near the goal, then returns to the thrower. A free throw curves out to a maximum range and comes back.
cards.behavior: Up to five distinct actors can be locked before the throw. At the throw the speed is set to a fixed value. With targets, the projectile steers toward the current target by a turn limit per update. The limit is a base plus a term that grows as the distance falls under about ten speeds, and it is fixed at a quarter turn in aimed mode. When it reaches a target (or hits it) it is turned about 67 degrees off the line to the next goal, so it swings out before it curves in, then aims at the next target. When all targets are done, or a shield is hit, it flips to the return phase, which aims at the catch point and is caught inside two steps of distance. A free throw with no lock aims at a point at maximum range along the aim direction, starts rotated about 67 degrees off the line so the path curves, and turns around once it gets there. Maximum range is doubled on a boat and in one boss stage.

cards.name: Target candidate scoring from a distance table
cards.summary: Each target type refers to a row of a distance table. A candidate must pass a vertical window, a facing-cone test and a radius that grows when the target is in front. The best candidates are the ones with the lowest angle-weighted distance divided by the row weight.
cards.behavior: Each candidate uses a row from the distance table. The row holds an acquire radius on the ground plane, a longer release radius, a front-angle bonus radius, a vertical window above and below the player, a weight divisor and a cone flag set. A candidate that fails the cone flag, the vertical window or the radius gets weight zero. The radius is the acquire radius plus the bonus radius times the square of one minus the angle fraction, so a target straight ahead is allowed far, and one behind is allowed only the base radius. The score is the distance times one half plus one half of the squared angle fraction, then divided by the row weight divisor, and the lowest scores win. Up to eight lock candidates are kept, with the worst replaced when a better one arrives. The cone flag values map to 90, 45 and 15 degree half angles from the player facing.

cards.name: Lock hold with a longer release radius
cards.summary: Once locked, a target is kept until it passes the longer release radius, the vertical window or the cone, so the lock does not flicker at the edge of the acquire range.
cards.behavior: Every update the held target is scored again like a fresh candidate. If it still scores above zero, the lock continues with the new weight. If not, a second test runs: the event conditions must hold, the cone must pass, and the distance test uses the release radius instead of the acquire radius. Passing that keeps the lock with a fresh weight. Failing it clears the lock and sets the lost flags. The release radius reported to other systems is the angle-adjusted bonus radius plus the release radius, so the camera and projectiles know when the lock will drop.

cards.name: Lock-on camera: obstruction swing, latitude limits and forced lock
cards.summary: The lock-on camera eases toward a framing of player and target with a smoothing factor. When the view is blocked or the player leaves the frame, it counts down a timer, pulls in to a fixed radius and swings sideways. Pitch is clamped. A forced lock on a thrown object ends by distance or by time.
cards.behavior: The camera keeps a center that tracks the player with a cushion factor that blends toward a target value each update. Longitude offset ramps in over a fixed number of updates after a lock begins. When the player is out of sight, or a line from the center to the player hits level geometry, a block timer is set. For that time the camera orbit radius eases toward a short radius, the center rises a little, and the heading swings by a fixed angle to one side. The pitch is clamped between a lower and an upper limit. A forced lock-on (used for a launched cannon shot, for example) is dropped when the normal lock starts, when the lock is older than the time limit, or when the object is farther than the distance limit. The source marks the decompiled lock-on camera function as not matching the original binary, so small details could differ.

cards.name: World wind: stage strength level and settable direction
cards.summary: One wind vector and one strength drive the sky, the sail and the leaf glide. A stage chooses one of three base strengths. A conducting event or a script sets the direction as two angles. The live value eases toward the target each update.
cards.behavior: The target direction is built from two stored angles as cosine and sine products, so it can point in any 3D direction. The target strength comes from a per-stage wind level: level 0, 1 and 2 map to three increasing values, and anything else gives zero. An event can force the wind off. A custom strength overrides the level. Strength is capped at one. The live vector eases toward the target by one tenth of the gap per update, with a step cap of 2 on each axis and a minimum step of 0.001, and the live strength eases by one tenth with a step cap of 1 and a minimum step of 0.005. Compass readouts divide the heading into eight sectors of 45 degrees each, with sector zero split across the start and end of the circle.

cards.name: Ocean height field from four traveling waves
cards.summary: The sea is a grid of heights that follows the player. Each height is a sum of four cosine waves of fixed amplitude, scaled by a per-sector wave setting and a flatten blend, with the outer cells scaled down toward zero height.
cards.behavior: The grid has 65 by 65 points, 800 units apart, centered on the player and covering plus or minus 25600 units. Each update the four waves advance by a counter that wraps at its own period (180 to 210 updates). Each wave has a wavenumber, a phase and a travel direction, and a base amplitude. The height at a point is the sum of the four cosines times their amplitudes, plus a base height, multiplied by a fade that drops to zero over the six outer grid cells on each side. The four wavelengths are about 13600, 11200, 8800 and 6400 units (derived from the wavenumbers). The amplitude scale is the product of a flatten factor and the wave setting of the 100000 unit sector under the player, eased by one hundredth per update. The default wave setting is 10. The height at any world point is interpolated from the surrounding grid points, and falls back to the base height outside the grid. The flatten factor drops toward zero as the player nears a sector whose wave setting is zero, which calms the sea.

cards.name: Boat speed from wind strength and heading
cards.summary: With the sail up, the target boat speed is a full-speed constant times a wind strength term that saturates at half strength, times a heading factor that falls as the boat turns into the wind. Speed approaches the target slowly. Raising the sail gives a short lunge.
cards.behavior: The heading factor starts at one when the boat runs downwind and falls linearly to about 0.75 at a quarter turn off the wind. From a quarter turn to three eighths of a turn it falls to about 0.3, and past that it falls steeply to zero within a few degrees, so sailing straight into the wind gives no push. The strength term is wind strength over one half, capped at one, so the middle wind level already gives full strength. Target speed is strength term times heading factor times the full-speed constant. While the sail raise animation passes its seventh frame, the speed jumps to twice the target, capped, if it is below that. Afterward speed chases the target by one tenth of the gap per update, with a step range. Coasting down is much slower: a twentieth of the gap, at most 0.1 per update. With the sail down in steering mode, the target is ten times the forward stick component. In the plain paddle mode it is ten times the analog trigger. The three wind levels give strength terms of 0.6, 1 and 1.

cards.name: Boat turn rate falls with speed; tiller eases toward the stick
cards.summary: The stick sets a tiller angle that eases toward its target. The heading turns by the tiller times a turn rate, and the turn rate drops as the boat gets faster. After a jump landing the turn rate is restored for a while.
cards.behavior: The tiller target is the sideways stick push times a fixed tiller range. The tiller chases the target by one quarter of the gap per update with a maximum and a minimum step. The heading change per update is the tiller (shifted down six bits) times a turn rate. The turn rate is a high value minus a share of speed, clamped to a range, so a fast boat turns in wide arcs and a slow boat turns sharply. At full tiller this gives about 460 binary angle units (2.5 degrees) per update when slow and about 128 (0.7 degrees) at full speed (derived). After a jump landing a timer holds the turn rate at the top of the range, and then blends it back to the speed value over the last 15 updates of the timer. A second spring-damper drives the visual lean toward the commanded turn.

cards.name: Boat height spring and pitch and roll from four wave probes
cards.summary: The boat rides a spring toward the water surface with a speed-scaled gain, a vertical-speed clamp and a random bob. Pitch and roll come from the water height at four points around the hull.
cards.behavior: Each update the height target is the sea height at the boat, or the stage water height when higher. Height moves a fraction of the error that scales with speed up to full speed, and a vertical speed gains a small fraction of the error, is clamped, and decays. A random bob phase and a small offset keep it moving. The height is clamped within a window above and below the surface. Pitch and roll are found from the height at four points around the hull (front, back, left, right), using the slope between each pair. A second spring turns that slope into the displayed tilt with a stiffness and a damping step, plus a speed-scaled random wobble. A jump has its own flight state until the boat hits the water.

cards.name: Boat jump off a wave: speed gate, launch speed and landing penalty
cards.summary: At high forward speed with the sail up, the lock button launches the boat. The vertical launch speed follows the sail speed between a floor and a ceiling. Landing bleeds forward speed and caps the impact.
cards.behavior: The jump is allowed only with the sail up after its raise animation, no event running, the measured forward speed above a threshold, and a sail target speed above a second threshold. A press of the right lock trigger then sets a flight state and sets the vertical speed equal to the target speed, clamped between a floor and a ceiling. A scale for the effect is derived from that speed. On touching the surface again the vertical speed is limited to a maximum downward value, forward speed is multiplied by a landing factor, and the turn boost timer starts.

cards.name: Boat collision: speed clamp, knock-off and tilt kick
cards.summary: A hit clamps and cuts the boat speed, throws the rider off unless protected, and kicks the pitch and roll springs. A cool-down stops repeat hits for 30 updates.
cards.behavior: Outside cutscenes, a crash throws the player off the boat unless they are invulnerable or the boat is under forced movement. Separately, if the cool-down is zero, boat speed is capped at the full sail speed and then multiplied by a damping factor. The hit angle relative to the heading splits a fixed kick between the pitch and roll angles, and the cool-down is set to 30 updates. While the cool-down is above zero, further crash calls only count it down.

cards.name: Deck cannon: fixed muzzle speed and short gravity-free flight
cards.summary: The cannon fires a bomb with a fixed muzzle speed along the barrel angle. Gravity is off for a few updates and then stays low. The camera follows the shot.
cards.behavior: When the cannon fire frame arrives, a bomb is created at the muzzle. Its forward speed is the cosine of the barrel pitch times the muzzle speed, and its vertical speed is the sine of the pitch times the muzzle speed, with the sign set by the angle convention. The bomb has no gravity for a short timer and then falls under a fixed gravity. The camera is forced to follow it, which relies on the forced lock limits of the lock-on camera. Firing costs one bomb from the inventory.
